scope: Saved football regression guards; no resimulation, NFL calibration or cost measurement.

comparisonPolicy.physicalHashes: Python canonical hashes of the retained JSON fields; not the engine opaque full signature.
comparisonPolicy.opaqueSignatureChange: The unchanged tackle tool includes a private perception ring in its full signature. Its storage stride changes from 6 to 7 and observed pose is added. A changed full signature alone is not proof of changed motion. Unexposed full-signature components cannot be reconstructed here.
comparisonPolicy.observations: Every observed diagnostic difference is retained. Pose differences use the reported column table, indexed into diagnostics[diagnosticIndex].perceivedCarrier[perceivedCarrierReadIndex].seen.pose. Presence flags distinguish absent from null. Other differences retain exact paths and values.
comparisonPolicy.metadata: Engine source and file hashes are retained separately. Run timestamps, command output paths and wall/CPU measurements are not interpreted as physics changes.

limits: All paired runs share initial inputs, roster profiles and seeds; later decisions and draws may diverge.
Run gains are offense-credited outcomes, not unpenalized physical gain. A defensive fumble returner can own first carrier contact.
The 64 tackle encounters reuse geometry. Exact retained physical paths are regression controls, not fresh tackle-rate evidence.
A live six-second tackle endpoint is a censor, not a forced failure or engine timeout.
Two games share initial seeds and roster only; later playcalls, trajectories and RNG consumption can diverge.
Small controlled panels and two games cannot demonstrate NFL significance, league means or computational speed.
Residual and motor-limit checks validate recorded accounting, not the correctness of all football mechanics.
